'''Archie Lee Goodwin III''' (born August 17, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Changwon LG Sakers]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].

==High school career==
Goodwin attended [[Sylvan Hills High School]] in [[Sherwood, Arkansas]] where he played for coach Kevin Davis and led his team to back-to-back state finals. As a junior in 2010–2011, his bid for a championship came up short when his team fell to [[Alma High School (Arkansas)|Alma High School]] from [[Alma, Arkansas]]. As a senior in 2011–12, Goodwin led the Bears to the Arkansas Class 5A [[List of Arkansas state high school basketball champions|state championship]], scoring 27 points and seven rebounds in the title game; winning championship and tournament [[Most valuable player|MVP]] honors along the way. Goodwin was twice named the [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] for Arkansas and named to the [[2012 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's]] and [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] teams.

Goodwin was rated as the number 15 player in the class of 2012 in the [[ESPNU]] 100,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/playerrankings/_/view/espnu100/sort/rank/class/2012|title=2012 College Basketball Recruiting Rankings - ESPNU 100|work=ESPN.com|access-date=December 3, 2011}}</ref> the number 9 player by [[Scout.com]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2012|title=Scout.com College Basketball Team Recruiting Prospects|work=Scout.com|access-date=December 3, 2011}}</ref> and the number 12 player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name=rivals>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2509;_ylt=AiI6gfIcQUepfUTytuUWMB3WO5B4|title=The Rivals150 2012 Prospect Rankings|work=Rivals.com|access-date=December 3, 2011}}</ref>

Goodwin chose Kentucky over offers from [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], among many others.

===Awards and honors===
* 2011 Arkansas Class 5A State Finalist, and All-Tournament Team
* 2011 and 2012 Arkansas Class 5A All-State Team
* 2011 and 2012 Arkansas [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]]
* 2011 and 2012 Arkansas McDonald's Full Court Awards Player of the Year
* 2011 and 2012 [[Mr. Basketball of Arkansas]] (''[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]'')
* 2012 Arkansas Class 5A State Championship, Championship Game MVP, and All-Tournament Team and MVP
* 2012 [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]
* 2012 [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]
* 2012 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] / USA Basketball Junior Select Team
* 2012 [[ESPN Rise boys' high school basketball All-Americans|ESPN HS Boys' Basketball All-American]] (Third Team)

==College career==
Goodwin was the leading scorer for the [[2012–13 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team]]. He was named Freshman All-SEC<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.local8now.com/home/headlines/2013-SEC-Mens-basketball-awards-announced-197391081.html|title=2013 SEC Men's basketball awards announced|work=local8now.com|date=March 12, 2013|access-date=April 1, 2013}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> after leading Kentucky with 14.1 points per game in 33 appearances (33 starts). He also averaged 4.6 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.1 steals to help the Wildcats to a 21–12 record. He tallied a career-high 28 points on 8-of-13 shooting and 12-of-17 free throws against [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]] on November 21.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire/_/section/ncb/id/8662129|title=No. 8 Kentucky holds off Morehead State 81-70|work=ESPN.com|date=November 21, 2012|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he narrowly missed the second triple-double in UK history against [[LIU Sharks men's basketball|LIU-Brooklyn]] with 22 points and career highs of nine rebounds and nine assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323280096|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030000219/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323280096|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 30, 2016|title=Kentucky overcomes slow start to defeat LIU|work=ESPN.com|date=November 23, 2012|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref>

On April 1, 2013, Goodwin declared for the [[2013 NBA draft]]. He was the second-youngest player to declare for the 2013 draft behind Greece's [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] and the youngest-overall American college player.<ref>{{cite web|first=Maxwell|last=Ogden|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1589364-archie-goodwin-declaring-for-the-nba-draft-was-only-option-for-kentucky-guard|title=Archie Goodwin: Declaring for the NBA Draft Was Only Option for Kentucky Guard|work=BleacherReport.com|date=April 1, 2013|access-date=April 1, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Phoenix Suns (2013–2016)===

====2013–14 season====
On June 27, 2013, Goodwin was chosen by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the 29th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. His rights were then traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]], before finally to the [[Phoenix Suns]], all on draft night.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/6/27/4468226/nba-draft-2013-phoenix-suns-archie-goodwin|title=NBA Draft 2013: Phoenix Suns select Archie Goodwin with No. 29 pick|work=SBNation.com|publisher=SB-Nation|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref> On July 12, 2013, he signed his [[rookie scale contract]] with the Suns and joined them for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://arizonasports.com/story/17325/phoenix-suns-sign-draft-pick-archie-goodwin/|title=Phoenix Suns sign draft pick Archie Goodwin|work=ArizonaSports.com|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}}</ref> In his first [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] game, Goodwin recorded 13 points and 3 rebounds against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130713/PHXPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Recap: Suns 82, Trail Blazers 69|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2013|access-date=July 13, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130712025708/http://www.nba.com/games/20130713/PHXPOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=July 12, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On October 30, 2013, Goodwin made his NBA debut against the Portland Trail Blazers. In 8 minutes of action, Goodwin attempted three shots and grabbed one offensive rebound. Goodwin, known as an aggressive scorer in college, went scoreless in his NBA debut. However, in Goodwin's second game against the [[Utah Jazz]] on November 1, he scored his first NBA field goal. In 11 minutes of action, Goodwin shot 2-of-5 from the field and ended with 4 points; he also recorded 2 blocks. On November 19, 2013, he recorded his first double-digit-scoring game with 16 points in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131119/PHXSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins' double-double rallies Kings past Suns|work=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2013|access-date=November 20, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131123185532/http://www.nba.com/games/20131119/PHXSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 23, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 23, 2014, Goodwin was assigned to the [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15110|title=Phoenix Suns assign Archie Goodwin to D-League|work=InsideHoops.com|date=January 23, 2014|access-date=January 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140710071721/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15110|archive-date=July 10, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was recalled on January 26,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15127|title=Suns recall Archie Goodwin from D-League|work=InsideHoops.com|date=January 26, 2014|access-date=January 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140710003448/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15127|archive-date=July 10, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> reassigned on February 5,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15181|title=Suns re-assign Archie Goodwin to D-League|work=InsideHoops.com|date=February 5, 2014|access-date=February 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140710010608/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15181|archive-date=July 10, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> and recalled again on February 10.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-recall-goodwin-bakersfield|title=Suns Recall Goodwin from Bakersfield|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2014|access-date=February 10, 2014}}</ref> In the Suns' final game of the season, Goodwin scored a career-high 29 points in a 104–99 win over the Sacramento Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140416/PHXSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Goodwin helps Suns to 104-99 win over Kings|work=NBA.com|date=April 17, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419040647/http://www.nba.com/games/20140416/PHXSAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 19, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2014–15 season====
After managing just 10 games for the Suns to start the season, Goodwin was reassigned to the Bakersfield Jam on December 25, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-assign-three-bakersfield|title=Suns Assign Three to Bakersfield|work=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2014|access-date=December 26, 2014}}</ref> He was recalled six days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-recall-ennis-goodwin-warren-bakersfield|title=Suns Recall Ennis, Goodwin, Warren from Bakersfield|work=NBA.com|date=December 31, 2014|access-date=December 31, 2014}}</ref> He was later reassigned to the Jam several more times during the season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628235947/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 28, 2015|title=2014-15 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> as he helped the Jam win the inaugural D-League Showcase championship and won the Showcase Tournament's MVP award on January 19.<ref>{{cite web|first=Sean|last=Sullivan|url=http://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2015/1/19/7854093/archie-goodwin-named-nba-d-league-showcase-cup-championship-mvp|title=Archie Goodwin Named NBA D-League Showcase Cup Championship MVP|work=BrightSideOfTheSun.com|publisher=SB-Nation|date=January 19, 2015|access-date=January 19, 2015}}</ref> He once again had an impressive regular season finale for the Suns, scoring a season-high 18 points in a loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/goodwar01/gamelog/2015/|title=Archie Goodwin 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
To begin the 2015–16 season, Goodwin saw limited court time aside from a 12-point, 17-minute outing in the team's season opener, which saw the Suns routed by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] at home. Over the next seven games, Goodwin averaged 6.9 minutes per game, competing for court time with new additions to the team in [[Devin Booker]] and [[Sonny Weems]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Gerald|last=Bourguet|url=http://hoopshabit.com/2015/11/18/phoenix-suns-archie-goodwin-earning-coach-hornaceks-trust/|title=Phoenix Suns: Archie Goodwin Earning Coach Hornacek's Trust|work=HoopsHabit.com|publisher=Fansided|date=November 18, 2015|access-date=November 18, 2015}}</ref> He later had two 12-point games in mid-November, both of which he played over 24 minutes in. He did not see regular court time for the Suns until early January following the injury to [[Eric Bledsoe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/goodwar01/gamelog/2016/|title=Archie Goodwin 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> On January 21, 2016, he scored a season-high 20 points as a starter in a loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160121/SASPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Spurs cruise to 12th straight win, 117-89 win over Suns|work=NBA.com|date=January 22, 2016|access-date=January 22, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he topped that mark with 24 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. In that game, Goodwin hit a three-pointer from atop the arc with 0.1 seconds left to lift the Suns over the Hawks with a 98–95 win, ending a six-game losing streak.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160123/ATLPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Goodwin hits 3 with 0.1 seconds left, Suns beat Hawks 98-95|work=NBA.com|date=January 24, 2016|access-date=January 24, 2016}}</ref> He topped his season-high mark for a third game in a row on January 26, scoring 26 points in a loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160126/PHXPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Smith, Covington lift suddenly decent 76ers past Phoenix|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2016|access-date=January 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408104542/http://www.nba.com/games/20160126/PHXPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 8, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 2, he recorded 18 points and had a career-high 12 assists in a 104–97 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160202/TORPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Lowry, Raptors hold off Suns, spoil Watson's coaching debut|work=NBA.com|date=February 2, 2016|access-date=February 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203214747/http://www.nba.com/games/20160202/TORPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 3, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 10, in a game against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Goodwin and teammate [[Markieff Morris]] got into a physical altercation on the bench and were seen arguing during a timeout. The argument escalated into a shoving match between the pair, as teammates quickly stepped in and separated the two.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/14757505|title=Markieff Morris, Archie Goodwin in shoving match during timeout|date=February 11, 2016|work=ESPN.com|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref>

Goodwin was released by the Suns on October 24, 2016, prior to the start of the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17]] regular season, in a move that was considered unexpected by many in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|title=Phoenix Suns Waive Archie Goodwin, Reduce Roster to 15|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-waive-archie-goodwin-reduce-roster-15|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 28, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Waived">{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Zimmerman|url=http://arizonasports.com/story/875311/suns-release-archie-goodwin/|title=Suns release guard Archie Goodwin, retain Jenkins and Jones Jr.|work=ArizonaSports.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> It was suggested that the Suns already had plenty of guards that needed some playing time as it was, and that there wasn't enough time for Goodwin to be fully satisfied in the process.<ref>{{cite web|first=James|last=Herbert|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/why-did-the-suns-and-celtics-cut-archie-goodwin-and-r-j-hunter/|title=Why did the Suns and Celtics cut Archie Goodwin and R.J. Hunter?|work=CBSSports.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> However, it was later confirmed by general manager [[Ryan McDonough (NBA executive)|Ryan McDonough]] that Goodwin had originally asked the team to try to trade him if it were possible, but the Suns couldn't find a team to help him out before the start of the regular season.<ref name="Waived"/>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2016)===
On November 7, 2016, Goodwin signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-archie-goodwin|title=Pelicans sign Archie Goodwin|work=NBA.com|date=November 7, 2016|access-date=November 7, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the Pelicans five days later, scoring seven points off the bench in a 126–99 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899579|title=Clarkson, Williams, lead Lakers past Pelicans, 126-99|work=ESPN.com|date=November 12, 2016|access-date=November 16, 2016}}</ref> On November 20, he was waived by the Pelicans after appearing in three games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-archie-goodwin|title=Pelicans waive Archie Goodwin|work=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm (2016–2017)===
On November 30, 2016, Goodwin was acquired by the [[Greensboro Swarm]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://greensboro.dleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-acquire-archie-goodwin/|title=Greensboro Swarm Acquire Archie Goodwin|work=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=December 2, 2016}}</ref> The next day, he made his debut for the Swarm in a 121–106 loss to the [[Texas Legends]], recording 18 points, six rebounds and one assist in 29 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20161201/GBOTEX/|title=Legends Cruise Past Swarm|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2016|access-date=December 2, 2016|archive-date=December 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203003505/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20161201/GBOTEX/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2017)===
On March 15, 2017, Goodwin signed a 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/03/15/nets-sign-archie-goodwin|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN ARCHIE GOODWIN TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=March 15, 2017|access-date=March 15, 2017}}</ref> He went on to sign a second 10-day contract on March 25,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/03/25/brooklyn-nets-sign-archie-goodwin-to-second-10-day-contract|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN ARCHIE GOODWIN TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2017|access-date=March 25, 2017}}</ref> and a multi-year contract on April 4.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/2017/04/04/brooklyn-nets-sign-archie-goodwin-multi-year-contract|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN ARCHIE GOODWIN TO MULTI-YEAR CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2017|access-date=April 4, 2017}}</ref> In the Nets' season finale on April 12, 2017, Goodwin scored a season-high 20 points in a 112–73 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/goodwar01/gamelog/2017/|title=Archie Goodwin 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=July 28, 2017}}</ref> On July 28, 2017, he was waived by the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/07/28/nets-waive-archie-goodwin|title=NETS WAIVE ARCHIE GOODWIN|work=NBA.com|date=July 28, 2017|access-date=July 28, 2017}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm and Northern Arizona Suns (2017–2018)===
On September 11, 2017, Goodwin signed a training camp contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-archie-goodwin|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN ARCHIE GOODWIN|work=NBA.com|date=September 11, 2017|access-date=September 11, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Trail Blazers on October 13, 2017, after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-briscoe-goodwin-and-morrow/|title=TRAIL BLAZERS WAIVE BRISCOE, GOODWIN AND MORROW|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2017|access-date=October 31, 2017}}</ref>

In the 2017–18 season, Goodwin split time between the [[Greensboro Swarm]] and the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].

===Maine Red Claws (2019)===
On October 19, 2018, he was traded to the [[Maine Red Claws]] in exchange for the rights to [[Daniel Dixon (basketball)|Daniel Dixon]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Friday's Sports Digest: Red Claws make moves before G League draft|url=https://www.pressherald.com/2018/10/19/fridays-sports-digest-red-claws-make-moves-before-g-league-draft/|access-date=October 22, 2018|work=[[Portland Press-Herald]]|date=October 19, 2018}}</ref> but did not make the team's final roster. On January 3, 2019, Goodwin re-signed with the Red Claws.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Boston|first1=Evans|title=Archie Goodwin Joins Red Claws|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/archie-goodwin-010319/|website=NBA G League|access-date=January 3, 2019|date=January 3, 2019|archive-date=January 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190104021559/https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/archie-goodwin-010319/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Sigortam.net İTÜ BB (2019–2020)===
On September 30, 2019, Goodwin signed with [[İstanbul Teknik Üniversitesi B.K.|Sigortam.net İTÜ BB]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketfaul.com/haber?haber=83543|title=Sigortam.net İTÜ'ye NBA patentli skorer|date=September 30, 2019|publisher=Basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=September 30, 2019}}</ref>

=== Ratiopharm Ulm (2020) ===
On February 6, 2020, Goodwin signed with [[Ratiopharm Ulm]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ulm-signs-archie-goodwin/|title=Ulm signs Archie Goodwin|work=Sportando |date=February 6, 2020|language=En|access-date=February 7, 2020 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> He averaged 7.0 points and 5.0 rebounds per game before the season was suspended.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Varney |first1=Dennis |title=Catch up with 36 ex-Cats playing pro basketball in leagues outside the NBA |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article241420196.html |access-date=May 16, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref>

=== Metropolitans 92 (2020–2021) ===
On November 25, 2020, Goodwin signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/archie-goodwin-joins-metropolitans-92/|title=Archie Goodwin joins Metropolitans 92|work=Sportando |date=November 25, 2020|language=En|access-date=November 26, 2020 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He averaged 8.7 points and 2.0 rebounds per game.<ref name="Budivelnyk" />

=== Budivelnyk (2022) ===
On January 8, 2022, Goodwin signed with [[BC Budivelnyk|Budivelnyk]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball Super League]].<ref name="Budivelnyk">{{cite web |last1=Cherkasov |first1=Sergey |title=Budivelnyk tabs Archie Goodwin, ex Levallois |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/725431/Budivelnyk-tabs-Archie-Goodwin,-ex-Levallois |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 8, 2022 |date=January 8, 2022}}</ref> He left the team in February 2022 in the [[prelude to the Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=John Stockton's son and his American teammate Archie Goodwin left Ukrainian basketball team before invasion|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/basketball/2022/02/24/john-stockton-son-archie-goodwin-flee-ukraine-russia/6924960001/|access-date=February 24, 2022|website=USA Today}}</ref>

=== Maccabi Rishon LeZion (2022) ===
On February 23, 2022, Goodwin signed with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Katsnelson |first1=Meidan |title=Archie Goodwin signed with Maccabi Rishon Le-Zion |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/732810/Archie-Goodwin-signed-with-Maccabi-Rishon-Le-Zion |website=Eurobasket |access-date=February 23, 2022 |date=February 23, 2022}}</ref>

=== Return to Budivelnyk (2022–2023) ===
On July 31, 2022, he has signed with [[BC Budivelnyk]] of the [[European North Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://budivelnyk.ua/index.php?route=blog/blog&blog_id=1381|title=Archie Goodwin for another season with Budivelnyk!|last=|first=|date=July 31, 2022|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 15, 2022}}</ref>

=== El Calor de Cancún (2024) ===
On August 13, 2024, he joined [[El Calor de Cancún]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]].<ref>{{cite web |title=El ex NBA, Archie Goodwin llega a El Calor de Cancún |url=https://deportesquintanaroo.com/2024/08/13/el-ex-nba-archie-goodwin-llega-a-el-calor-de-cancun/ |publisher=Deportes Quintana Roo |access-date=August 18, 2024 |date=August 13, 2024}}</ref>

=== Jiangsu Dragons (2024-2025) ===
On October 20, 2024, Goodwin signed with [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AND ONE！欢迎阿奇·古德温加入肯帝亚大家庭！ |url=https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20241020A076NJ00 |website=腾讯新闻 |access-date=October 24, 2024 |date=October 20, 2024}}</ref>

=== Taipei Fubon Braves (2025–2026) ===
On August 22, 2025, Goodwin signed with the [[Taipei Fubon Braves]] of the [[P. League+]].<ref>{{cite web |title=台籃又有NBA等級戰將 富邦勇士簽約前太陽古德溫 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3020081 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=July 3, 2026 |date=August 22, 2025}}</ref>

=== Changwon LG Sakers (2026–present) ===
On July 3, 2026, Goodwin signed with the [[Changwon LG Sakers]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=프로농구 LG, NBA 드래프트 1R 출신 굿윈 영입 |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20260703080600007 |website=연합뉴스 |access-date=July 3, 2026 |date=July 3, 2026}}</ref>
